title: add-benchmark-lab-profiling-baselines-and-reporting-pipeline-v67
author: Evelyn Chen
release_notes: Add profiling baselines, representative workload runners, and reporting pipeline v67 for Benchmark Lab. Improves cold-start profiling coverage and adds multi-variant reporting summaries.
description:
Motivation: Benchmark Lab needs more representative profiling baselines and an automated reporting pipeline to track regressions across multi-variant runs (models, quantization, sequence lengths). This PR implements profiling baselines V67, adds mixed and conversational workload runners, standardizes result schema, and wires a nightly reporting pipeline.

What this PR does: - Adds profiling baselines in benchmark-lab/profiling/baselines/v67/ with standardized YAML metadata for run reproducibility. - Adds new runners: mixed_workload_runner.py (latency/throughput mixed traffic), conv_chat_runner.py (multi-turn conversational workload). - Implements result normalization and delta calculation utilities for reporting. - Adds a lightweight reporting pipeline (airflow DAG + reporting script) that aggregates daily runs, computes regression deltas, and uploads CSV/JSON artifacts to the internal benchmark bucket. - Adds dashboard metadata files and example queries for the Console.

Checklist: - [x] Add baseline data schema and example manifests - [x] Implement runners with unit tests and small integration smoke tests - [x] Add reporting DAG and notification hook (slack) - [x] Update docs/README for running locally - [x] Add canary job for dedicated infra

Commits summary: - "init: add v67 profiling baselines and schema" - "feat(runners): mixed and conversational workload runners with prefix/KV warmup" - "feat(reporting): nightly DAG + normalization utilities" - "test: add unit+integration tests for runners and reporting" - "chore: docs and example queries"

Files changed (high level): - benchmark-lab/profiling/baselines/v67/baseline_manifest.yaml - benchmark-lab/runners/mixed_workload_runner.py - benchmark-lab/runners/conv_chat_runner.py - benchmark-lab/reporting/dags/profiling_report_v67.py - benchmark-lab/reporting/normalize_results.py - benchmark-lab/tests/test_mixed_runner.py - benchmark-lab/tests/test_reporting.py - docs/benchmark-lab/v67.md

Notes on implementation: - Runners include an optional --kv-warmup flag to populate KV cache before timed runs to isolate model cold-start vs KV-cache effects. - Baseline manifest supports per-variant quantization and hardware tags so the reporting pipeline can align comparable runs. - Reporting pipeline computes median P50/P95 token latency, tokens/sec, and a delta score relative to the stored baseline. Small helper ensures deterministic rounding for stable diffs.

CI summary: Initial CI run failed on one flaky integration test (test_reporting::test_upload) due to a transient GCS permission; I re-ran CI after adding a retry wrapper and the full suite passed. Checks: lint (pass), unit tests (pass), integration (pass after rerun), e2e smoke (pass), airflow-lint (pass).

Review discussion (high level): - Samir: "Can we avoid coupling the reporting DAG to GCS paths? Suggest parameterizing bucket via env var and add a fallback local-upload mode for on-prem." -> Reply: "Done, added REDWOOD_BENCH_BUCKET env var and local fallback for private deployments." - Priya: "Runner should expose per-request metadata for tracing and cost breakdown." -> Reply: "Added trace_id and cost_estimate metadata fields in runner output; updated tests." - Lina: "Please add retention policy for baseline artifacts." -> Reply: "Added retention_days to baseline_manifest and documented retention in v67.md."

Performance/regression notes: Early runs show ~3% median token latency improvement for BFloat16 quantized variants on A100 compared to v66, and a ~1.5% regression for an LLM variant on T4 under mixed workloads (investigation ticket created ENG-4398).

Backward compatibility: Result schema versions are bumped (v1 -> v2) but reporters include a compatibility shim so older dashboards can still read results; documented the shim and upgrade steps in the README.

Merge: Squash-merged to main after approvals and green CI.
